question.:question/problem:
![](images/7c/7cc0c8077c4ea0880d777ffe6fdbedff0d60a451a48c46e552bff71700f16df0.png)

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the ellipse shown above.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since our ellipse is centered at the origin and has semiaxes $1$ and $2,$ its equation is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}=1\,⟹\,{x}^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=1.
$$

Now, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}) & =0 \\ 2x+\frac{2y}{4}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ \frac{y}{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-2x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{4x}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

domain.coordinate_axis_convention: Coordinate axes x=0 and y=0 are allowed on the real locus. The derivative quotient excludes only y=k.

Since our ellipse is centered at $(-3,-3)$ and has semiaxes $1$ and $2,$ its equation is given by

$$
\frac{(x-(-3))^{2}}{{1}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-3))^{2}}{{2}^{2}}=1\,⟹\,(x+3)^{2}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{4}=1.

Now, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}((x+3)^{2}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{4}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}((x+3)^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{4}) & =0 \\ 2(x+3)+\frac{2(y+3)}{4}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ \frac{y+3}{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-2(x+3) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{4(x+3)}{y+3}\end{aligned}
$$
